thesis_summary.thesis: Limoneira Company is a California-based agribusiness founded in Santa Paula that farms, packs, and markets lemons and avocados while managing rental operations and real estate development on roughly **10,500** acres of owned land and water resources. **[Fact]** The company also farms internationally (Chile, Argentina, Arizona) on approximately **3,100** lemon acres, **1,500** avocado acres, **100** orange acres, and **400** wine-grape acres. **[Fact]** Three divisions report through SEC filings: agribusiness (fresh lemons, lemon packing, avocados, other), rental operations (residential/commercial leases and organic recycling), and real estate development (Harvest at Limoneira joint venture with Lewis Group and East Area II). **[Fact]** FY2025 revenue was **$159.7 million** (down from **$191.5 million** in FY2024); net income **$16.0 million** (up from **$7.7 million**); cash from operations **$6.0 million** (down from **$17.9 million**). **[Fact]** The stock traded at **~$11.83** on June 6, 2026 (Yahoo Finance), slightly above GAAP book of **~$10.70** per share on **~17.8 million** diluted shares.
thesis_summary.why_market_wrong: The market may price Limoneira as a cyclical lemon packer whose revenue fell **17%** year over year, missing the dated cash from **~$180 million** of expected development distributions and episodic water and land sales. **[Inference]** At **~$11.83**, the stock sits near GAAP book while **10,500** California acres, basin water rights, and entitled housing land are carried at historical cost. **[Fact]** Management reiterates a strategic pivot: Sunkist lemon partnership (shifting quarterly revenue cadence), **800** acres of non-bearing avocados coming into production, **~$10 million** targeted selling, general, and administrative savings, and near-term water monetization in fiscal 2026. **[Inference]** Predictive attribute: **land, water, and development yield curve** (known catalyst stack with lumpy ag transition noise).
